facts.fact_text: The applicant is a journalist.
Hyde Park organised a demonstration on 8 May 2008.
The applicant decided to go on hunger strike because he was unable to trace his brother for two days.
On 10 May 2008 at 10 a.m., the applicant stood outside the Government building in Chișinău's main square.
On 10 May 2008 at 10 a.m., the applicant positioned a placard with the inscription "Hunger strike for rights" outside the Government building in Chișinău's main square.
On 10 May 2008 at 10 a.m., the applicant started a silent protest outside the Government building in Chișinău's main square.
The applicant refused the order to stop filming and stated that he is a journalist on hunger strike.
Shortly after the applicant began his silent protest on 10 May 2008, police officers approached him.
At approximately 10.45 a.m. on 10 May 2008, the applicant was approached by two persons wearing plain clothes.
One of the two plain-clothed persons hit the applicant, apparently in the hand holding the camera.
One of the two plain-clothed persons threatened the applicant in rude terms with violence if he did not stop filming.
The second plain-clothed police officer appeared to forcefully put an end to the applicant's filming.
The second plain-clothed police officer seized the applicant by his clothes and hands.
Two uniformed police officers approached and apprehended the applicant.
The two uniformed police officers took the applicant to a police van without any resistance from the applicant.
The applicant arrived at the police station at approximately 11 a.m. on 10 May 2008.
The applicant's personal effects were taken away at the police station.
The applicant was detained for forty-eight hours in solitary confinement in a cell without windows.
At the Buiucani District Court on 12 May 2008, the applicant learned that he had been charged with the offence of insulting police officers.
At the Buiucani District Court on 12 May 2008, the applicant learned that he had been charged with the offence of resisting arrest.
At the end of the hearing on 12 May 2008, at 3 p.m., the applicant was released.
At the police station, the applicant discovered that the memory of his video camera (approximately forty-five minutes of film) had been erased.
According to Law No. 26 of 22 February 2008, in force at the time of the events, no authorisation is needed to hold a peaceful demonstration with fewer than fifty participants.

According to Article 249 of the Code of Administrative Offences of Moldova, persons who disobey in bad faith the lawful orders of police officers, or resist or insult police officers, may be detained until their case is examined by a court.
The second plain-clothed police officer retorted that by protesting the applicant was breaching the rights of other persons.
The police accused the applicant of calling them "rats", "cowards" and "Voronin's dogs" when they peacefully approached him.
The applicant was accused by the Minister of Internal Affairs of having provoked the police officers by insulting them and resisting arrest.
On 5 June 2008, the Buiucani District Court delivered its judgment acquitting the applicant of all charges.
The Buiucani District Court examined the videos of the applicant's encounter with the police and his arrest of 10 May 2008 before delivering its judgment.
The Buiucani District Court found that the accusations against the applicant were false.
The Buiucani District Court found that the applicant had not insulted the police officers.
The Buiucani District Court found that the applicant had not resisted arrest.
On 15 June 2008, the Chișinău Prosecutor's Office dismissed the applicant's appeal on the ground that the police officers' behaviour did not disclose an offence.
The Chișinău Prosecutor's Office noted that the applicant had insulted the police officers by calling them "rats", "cowards" and "Voronin's dogs".
The Chișinău Prosecutor's Office noted that the two police officers who had physically and verbally assaulted the applicant had been admonished for their behaviour.
According to Article 184 of the Criminal Code of Moldova, breach of the right to peaceful assembly by a public official is punishable with a fine, community service or up to two years' imprisonment.
According to Article 328 of the Criminal Code of Moldova, abuse of authority accompanied by acts of violence is punishable with up to ten years' imprisonment.
On 26 May 2008, the criminal complaint lodged by the applicant was dismissed by the Prosecutor's Office.
The applicant appealed against the dismissal of his criminal complaint.
In his appeal, the applicant added that he had been held in inhuman and degrading conditions.
In his appeal, the applicant added that he had not been provided with appropriate medical assistance.
The video of the applicant's verbal and physical abuse in front of the Government building became the subject matter of a media scandal.
Several television stations reported on the event of the applicant's verbal and physical abuse in front of the Government building and broadcast the video footage.
On 28 May 2008, the Minister of Internal Affairs formally admonished two police officers, C.A. and V.O.
Without any explanations, C.A. and V.O. received an admonishment for breaching several rules of police conduct, in particular unprofessional conduct, dishonesty and failure to identify themselves.
